overview: This table holds the words shown in the game's command list, including fighter descriptions, passive skills, and move names and explanations.
description: Localized command-list strings: one row supplies a character description, passive/attack name, or attack description. CommandListDataTable supplies the CMD_ ids, and the command-list widgets resolve them through the shared GameTextManager; attack descriptions receive an additional C++-side parser.

ID.simple: The name the command list uses to find this text for a fighter, passive skill, or move. Change it only with the matching command-list entry.
ID.technical: FName ID in FGameDataTableRow_GameText. All 11 exported shards have row keys equal to ID. Runtime FindRow uses FName(Request.TextId) as the row name; the lookup does not read the row's ID property, which FindTextIdsContaining instead reads for substring matching. CommandListDataTable owns the references in Id_CommandListText_CharacterDescription, paired Id_CommandListText_PassiveName/Description arrays, and named normal-, cursed-energy-, super-, and extra-attack name/description fields; Id_CommandListText_TagComboAttack_Name exists in the header but has no C++ consumer in this reconstruction. UGameCommandListWidget gates action slots on the name id being non-None, gates passive slots on valid paired array indices and both ids being non-None, and sends the character description to SetTextIdOnly without an IsNone gate; NAME_None requests clear the text block. Attack names use SetTextIdOnly and attack descriptions use GetText, while passive names are injected as SKILL_NAME request parameters behind SYS_COMMANDLIST_LABEL_0002. StartLanguageLoading loads CommandListTextDataTable_<Language> and Tick inserts it fourth (zero-based index 3) into the 14-table TextDataTables search order.

Text.simple: The words shown in the chosen language for a fighter description, skill name, or move explanation. Some move explanations also show Cursed Energy levels and small button symbols.
Text.technical: FString Text (+0x10) returned by value; a missing row returns an empty FString. GetGameText/GetText run FormatText over [MODS] tags: GLO keys resolve against GlossaryParameters (rebuilt from GlossaryTextDataTable_ rows keyed by row name), DYN keys against request parameters, unmatched tags remain unchanged, and recognized modifiers change number/format conversion. The En export has 51 GLO tag occurrences (27 distinct keys) and no DYN tags; no shard contains DYN tags, and every GLO key has a matching glossary row in its language. Action-widget descriptions are additionally parsed before display: split on the literal '' with empty pieces culled, then '【'/'[' opener and '】'/']' closer, ':' labels, line breaks, and ASCII/full-width 1/2/3 level digits build up to two message frames and two rows per level; exact ids CMD_COMMAND_DESCRIPTION_CP_170_4000, CMD_COMMAND_DESCRIPTION_CP_080_3000, and CMD_COMMAND_DESCRIPTION_CP_210_3000 have special branches. '' survives FormatText and is rendered by the rich-text inline decorator using a custom image-row brush; the description parser also has a special img-id line branch except for CP_170_4000. Name rows are not passed through this description parser. An existing row can hold empty text: all shards leave CMD_COMMAND_NAME_CP_210_7000 empty, and it is referenced only by CP_210's Id_CommandListText_TagComboAttack_Name, for which no C++ consumer was found.

notes: All 11 shards export the same 628 row keys with zero row-key/ID mismatches and one empty Text value (CMD_COMMAND_NAME_CP_210_7000). All 628 distinct non-None ids referenced by CommandListDataTable resolve in these rows; no row is orphaned in the export.

Same FGameDataTableRow_GameText struct and 11 language variants; exported strings differ by locale. Config/DefaultGame.ini:35-45 assigns cooked chunks with a shared TextDataTable_<Language> filter that also catches this table, not with table-specific entries.

Cross-table join: CommandListDataTable supplies ids, this table supplies strings, and GLO keys resolve through the GlossaryParameters map rebuilt from GlossaryTextDataTable_<Language> (verified present for every key in every shard). DYN keys come from request parameters; no DYN tags occur in this group. SYS_ ids bypass TextDataTables and are looked up in SystemTextDataTable.

Lookup precedence and refresh: FindTextRow scans the 14-table array in order (Glossary, Battle, Item, CommandList fourth, then the rest) and returns the first matching row name, so an earlier duplicate wins; there is no CMD_ prefix routing. Tick rebuilds TextDataTables and GlossaryParameters after all loaders complete, then clears the loader map; rich-text blocks keep their TextId/parameters and StudioLocalization2 re-resolves them after OnCultureTextLoaded.

'', full-width/ASCII brackets, level digits, and '' markup are ordinary characters in the exported FString; only UGameCommandListActionWidget's description path interprets them. The widget arrays hold two generic message frames and two rows per level, so a third section or a third level row has no destination and is skipped. An empty non-None id is not a hide sentinel; action visibility is driven by the CommandList name id being NAME_None, while the one empty-text row is attached to TagComboAttack_Name with no C++ consumer traced.

Reconstruction caveat: status/functions.json marks GetText/GetGameText/FormatText byte-matched and FindTextRow/Tick behaviour-certified (0x14af290 NA15, 0x14c96f0 BG03); SetupContent and BuildContents are behaviour-certified reconstructions, not byte matches. No retail Blueprint widget layout or animation was inspected, so visual presentation beyond these traced C++ consumers and exported strings remains unverified.

usages.detail: Sets the character explanation rich-text block to Id_CommandListText_CharacterDescription with no explicit IsNone gate.

Bounds-checks paired passive name/description arrays before indexing; later lines require both ids non-None, inject the name as SKILL_NAME into SYS_COMMANDLIST_LABEL_0002, and set the description directly.
Copies attack name and description ids into FGameCommandListActionParameter; each attack slot's visibility is set from its name id being non-None.
AttackName uses SetTextIdOnly; DescriptionTextId is fetched with GetText and then split/parsed into explanation frames.
Description parser handles img-id lines specially except for CMD_COMMAND_DESCRIPTION_CP_170_4000; later branches assign level labels/messages by ASCII or full-width digit.
Loads CommandListTextDataTable_<Language> as the fourth of 14 GameText tables put into TextDataTables by Tick.
FindTextRow returns the first table with a matching row name; GetGameText reads row Text at +0x10 and returns an empty string when no row is found.
SetTextIdOnly builds a request resolved by GameTextManager::GetText; StudioLocalization2 re-resolves the stored id and parameters after a culture change.
Rich-text decorator accepts runs when the id resolves to a brush in the custom image set, rendering markup left intact by FormatText.
